title: Calculating with measurements
keyIdea: Before you add or subtract measurements, put them in the same unit: 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 l = 1000 ml. Then calculate with the numbers and keep the unit on the answer. To find how much longer, heavier or more, find the difference.
familyTip: Measure two things with a ruler or tape and ask how long they would be end to end. Use a kitchen scale: weigh one item, add another and ask your child to say the new mass before reading the scale. When you pour a drink from a 1 litre carton, ask how much is left.

visual.caption: Add, or take away to find what is left or the difference? Drag each card to a box, or tap the card then a box.

bins: Take away or find the difference
items: Two ribbons of 45 cm and 38 cm joined
A 1 litre jug after pouring out 250 ml
A plant that grew from 23 cm to 41 cm
A 350 g bag and a 400 g bag on a scale
A 2 m rope with 60 cm cut off
A walk of 300 m and then 450 m more

lab.caption: Flagship lab: read mm, join ribbons, change 1 m 30 cm to cm before adding, read a 50 g scale, pour from 1 litre, count on to find growth.

kid: A ruler shows centimetres. Each centimetre has 10 tiny marks called millimetres. So 1 cm = 10 mm, and 7 cm and 4 mm is 74 mm.
To add two lengths, put them end to end. 45 cm and 38 cm make 83 cm. The 5 and 8 make 13, so you get a new ten.
You can only add things in the same unit. 1 m is 100 cm. So 1 m 30 cm is 130 cm. Add 85 cm and you get 215 cm.
Grams and millilitres work the same way. 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 litre = 1000 ml. Pour 250 ml two times from 1 litre and 500 ml is left.
adult: Ages 7 to 8. In England, Year 3 pupils measure, compare, add and subtract lengths in m, cm and mm, mass in kg and g, and capacity in l and ml. This builds on Year 2, where they chose units and compared measures with <, > and =.

Two rules carry most of the work. First, convert to one unit, using 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 l = 1000 ml. Second, use the usual written or mental methods and keep the unit on the answer. A difference, such as how much a plant grew, can be found by counting on from the smaller value.

Common mistakes: adding mixed units as if they were the same (1 m + 30 cm written as 31). Thinking 1 kg is 100 g. Reading every small mark on a scale as 1 when each one is worth 50. Forgetting the new ten made by the ones. Adding the two heights when the question asks how much more.

In the lab your child reads three lengths to the millimetre. They drag one ribbon to meet another and add the lengths. They change 1 m 30 cm to 130 cm before adding. They read a scale that counts in 50 g, pour two 250 ml glasses from a 1 litre jug, and hop along a number line to find how much a plant grew.

practice.prompt: A pencil ends 6 small marks after 9 cm on a ruler. How long is it?
practice.hint: Each cm is 10 mm, so 9 cm is 90 mm. Add the small marks.
practice.explain: 9 cm is 90 mm, and 6 more mm makes 96 mm.

practice.prompt: A ribbon is {a} cm long. Another is {b} cm long. How long are they end to end, in cm?
practice.hint: End to end means add the two lengths. Watch for a new ten from the ones.

practice.prompt: A jug holds 1 litre. You pour out {p} ml. How many ml are left?
practice.hint: 1 litre is 1000 ml. Take away what you poured.

practice.prompt: Ali says 1 m + 40 cm = 41 cm. What went wrong?
choices: He treated 1 m as 1 cm; it is 100 cm, so the answer is 140 cm
practice.hint: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
practice.explain: 1 m = 100 cm, so 1 m + 40 cm = 140 cm, or 1 m 40 cm.

practice.prompt: A bag of rice has a mass of {r} g. A bag of pasta has a mass of 500 g. What is the total mass in grams?
practice.hint: Both are in grams already, so add the numbers.

pool.prompt: How many grams are in 1 kg?
pool.hint: Kilo means a thousand, as in kilometre.

pool.prompt: A scale counts up in 50 g. The needle is one mark after 600 g. What is the mass?
pool.hint: Each small mark is worth 50 g here, not 1 g.
pool.explain: One 50 g mark after 600 g is 650 g.

pool.prompt: A plant was {a} cm tall. Now it is {b} cm tall. How many cm did it grow?
pool.hint: Find the difference: count on from {a} to {b}.

pool.prompt: What is 2 m 15 cm in centimetres?
pool.hint: Each metre is 100 cm, so change the metres first.
pool.explain: 2 m is 200 cm. 200 cm + 15 cm = 215 cm.

pool.prompt: 47 cm + 36 cm. Which answer is right?
pool.hint: 7 + 6 = 13 ones. That is 1 ten and 3 ones.
pool.explain: 40 + 30 = 70, and 7 + 6 = 13. 70 + 13 = 83 cm. 73 forgets the new ten.

pool.prompt: A bottle holds 1 litre. You drink 250 ml two times. How much is left?
pool.hint: 1 litre is 1000 ml. Two drinks of 250 ml are 500 ml.
pool.explain: 1000 ml − 500 ml = 500 ml, half a litre.

pool.prompt: How many millimetres are in {c} cm?
Mia adds 1 kg and 200 g and writes 201 g. What should she have done first?
choices: Change 1 kg to 1000 g, then add to get 1200 g
pool.hint: You can only add masses in the same unit.
